name: Button labels are specific, not vague
source: Krug DMMT Law #1 (self-evident labels) + Nielsen #2 (match real world) + Nielsen #4 (consistency)
description: Detects buttons with vague, generic, or technical labels: 'Submit', 'OK', 'Click here', 'Click', 'Button', 'Go', 'Send', when used as the primary action label. Specific labels like 'Save changes', 'Send invoice', 'Add to cart' tell the user what will happen.
rationale: Steve Krug's Law #1 ('Don't Make Me Think') says button labels should be self-evident — the user shouldn't have to guess what 'Submit' means. Nielsen heuristic #2 (Match between system and the real world) says to use the user's vocabulary, not technical jargon. 'Submit' is a holdover from HTML form spec; 'OK' communicates nothing about what's being OK'd. NN/g research on form usability consistently shows that descriptive button labels reduce form abandonment.
pass_criteria: Fewer than 3 buttons have a label that is exactly one of: Submit, OK, Click here, Click, Button, Go, Cancel (cancel is OK if there's a confirm/affirm button nearby), Send (alone), Done (alone).
